summary: When a positive #kick command reduces a mounted pony’s tameness and the resistance check fails, C calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_THROWN). JavaScript kick_steed records the missing dismount as unported, so the steed remains mounted and the later turn draws replace C’s landing_spot tie-break. The existing JavaScript landing_spot probe on the recorded pre-action state draws rn2(3), matching C; the divergence is the missing caller and DISMOUNT_THROWN branch, not candidate counting.

source.branch: The hero is mounted, answers yes to kicking, and after kick_steed decrements mtame the hero-level-plus-tameness resistance check fails.

evidence: The saved v52 evaluation identifies step 163 as the first screen and RNG mismatch: C records rn2(3)=1 at steed.c:landing_spot line 543, while JavaScript records rn2(5)=2 and leaves the screen cursor at [52,8,1] instead of [75,0,1].

Upstream steed.c:402-450 decrements the steed’s tameness and calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_THROWN) when tameness is zero or the resistance roll fails. js/steed.js:kick_steed instead records note_unported and returns at this branch.

Upstream steed.c:600-613 maps DISMOUNT_THROWN to the same fall message and riding-accident processing as DISMOUNT_FELL. js/steed.js:dismount_steed calls landing_spot before its reason switch but throws UnsupportedSteedError for DISMOUNT_THROWN, so the branch cannot complete.

A direct call to the existing JavaScript landing_spot on the pony replay’s visible pre-action state returns a single tie-break bound of 3, matching the C bound. The missing thrown dismount path explains why later JavaScript turn RNG replaces the C landing tie-break.
